# quicknode_chains (Data Source)

Every chain and network Quicknode supports. Use it to validate slugs at plan time and to fan a configuration out across networks.

Chain slugs are abbreviations that often differ from the chain's name: Ethereum is `eth`, Avalanche is `avax`, Arbitrum is `arb`, Polygon is `matic`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "quicknode_chains" "all" {}

# Chain slugs are abbreviations that often differ from the chain's name, so look
# one up instead of hardcoding it.
locals {
  ethereum = one([for chain in data.quicknode_chains.all.chains : chain if chain.slug == "eth"])
}

resource "quicknode_endpoint" "primary" {
  chain   = local.ethereum.slug
  network = one([for network in local.ethereum.networks : network.slug if network.chain_id == 1])
}
```

## Schema

### Read-Only

- `chains` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chains))

<a id="nestedatt--chains"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chains`

Read-Only:

- `is_select_chain` (Boolean) Whether the chain is only available on Quicknode's Select plans.
- `networks` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chains--networks))
- `slug` (String) Chain slug, as `quicknode_endpoint.chain` expects it.

<a id="nestedatt--chains--networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chains.networks`

Read-Only:

- `chain_id` (Number) EVM chain id, or null on non-EVM networks.
- `name` (String) Human-readable network name.
- `slug` (String) Network slug, as `quicknode_endpoint.network` expects it. Most are chain-qualified (`base-sepolia`), but some are not (`mainnet` for Ethereum, `bsc`, `optimism`).
